purpose: One human-launched finite native account, policy-projection, Codex-limit and model-catalog metadata observation; no model turn or scientific review.
authorized_native_effects: Before native credential access, one local synthetic bubblewrap test checks exact fake-file writes and parent/read-only-file denials. It uses no real credential or network request and stops the native check if it fails.

The pinned installed Codex client may read and update only the existing /home/afazeli2006/.codex/auth.json through a same-path writable file mount for its normal credential refresh. Its parent directory remains unwritable; parent Python never opens, hashes, copies or exports credential contents.
The bounded native process may use inherited host networking for account authentication/refresh and startup or requested metadata services. This is not an enforced network endpoint allowlist.

Existing configuration, managed-policy origins, cloud-policy/model caches, resolver and CA inputs are preserved as exact read-only file inputs. No HOME, CODEX_HOME, backend, account security or managed-policy setting is changed.

Other writable mounts are the fixed fresh project runtime directories and a private project-backed copy of the same existing nonsecret installation identifier. The original identifier is not writable.

The parent may send only initialize, initialized, config/read, configRequirements/read, account/read with refreshToken false, account/rateLimits/read and one model/list page. Native startup can perform its own metadata/authentication work.
Only filtered nonsecret report fields are shared. A completed report is reused, never remeasured merely because publication failed.
forbidden_actions: No assistant or parent access to credential values; no credential copy, backup, content hash, export, upload, publication or raw native output capture in a report.
No native login/logout or account replacement requested; no thread, model turn, prompt, scientific input, credit/reset consumption, paid API usage, purchases or new spending.
No full home/Codex-home write or read grant, session-bus socket, other-programme access, background supervisor or unattended model continuation.
No automatic retry, permission expansion, client upgrade, configuration repair, removal of a partial attempt or repeated completed observation.
limitations: Native credential persistence truncates and writes in place. Interruption or I/O failure during this native operation can leave an incomplete credential file; the wrapper does not copy credentials to conceal that client limitation.
A Codex limit response is not an authoritative hosted-ChatGPT allowance reading. A model catalog entry is not a successful model invocation or full entitlement proof.
Effective policy projection is observed but cloud-policy closure and the full scientific reviewer tool boundary remain unverified.
approval_protocol: After publishing checkpoint016, human appends one actual ## ANSWER section containing only APPROVE_G0_POSTLOGIN_016 and scope_sha256: <hash of this exact file> to state/ESCALATION.md, commits/pushes the answer, then launches the canonical script with --run-metadata. Default inspection needs no new approval.
